transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, uh, thank you for calling S-Net Billing and Account Support. My name is Zara speaking. Who am I speaking with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Zara, um, my name is Nafisa Begum. I just opened my final statement email and I am honestly shocked because you've billed me two hundred and forty pounds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh no, Nafisa, I am so sorry for the shock of seeing a two hundred and forty pound charge on your final statement, especially right after moving home.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, it really stressed me out because when I rang up last month to say I was moving, the advisor told me there wouldn't be a penalty if S-Net couldn't supply my new cottage.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand why that's upsetting, Nafisa, and I am going to sort this out for you myself right now. First, could you confirm your previous billing address and answer your security question, which is your first primary school?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, uh, my old address was Flat 4, 19 Clarendon Road, Leeds, LS2 9NZ, and my security question answer is Oakwood Primary.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Lovely, thank you Nafisa, that's all verified on your profile. So just to put this in my own words, after moving from Leeds to a rural area where S-Net has no network coverage, your closed account was erroneously charged a two hundred and forty pound early termination fee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exact—uh, exactly that! It says early contract cancellation fee for the remaining ten months of my Fibre 500 plan.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, let's get to the bottom of why the billing engine generated that fee. To start with, Nafisa, what is the full postcode and first line of the new rural property you moved into?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's Bryn Awel Cottage in Bethesda, near Bangor in North Wales, and the postcode is LL57 4BQ.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bryn Awel Cottage, LL57 4BQ—got it. How is the move to North Wales going so far apart from this billing headache?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Honestly, the mountains and the peace and quiet are wonderful, we're just still living out of cardboard boxes in the kitchen!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ha, unpacking the kitchen always takes twice as long as you think! Now, when you spoke to our home-move team before relocating to LL57 4BQ, did they give you a home-move check reference number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Um, let me look at the back of my notebook here... yes, I wrote down HM-774120 on the eighteenth of September.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, I see note HM-774120 from the eighteenth of September right here. And what date did you actually complete your move out of Flat 4, 19 Clarendon Road?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We handed the keys back to the letting agent in Leeds on the thirtieth of September, which was the exact disconnection date I requested.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, so the service at Clarendon Road ceased on the thirtieth of September. Did the advisor ask you to send in any proof of residency for LL57 4BQ, like a council tax letter or tenancy agreement?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I uploaded our Gwynedd Council Tax registration letter and the signed completion statement through the S-Net portal on the first of October.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check your document attachments... yes, I can see the Gwynedd Council Tax PDF uploaded on the first of October showing your name at Bryn Awel Cottage, LL57 4BQ.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's why I couldn't understand why the automated bill still slapped two hundred and forty pounds onto my account this morning!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me also check one more detail before I inspect the ledger coding—did you already return the S-Net Hub 5 router in the prepaid Royal Mail returns bag?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I posted the router back from the Bethesda post office on the second of October, and the Royal Mail tracking number is RM449012883GB.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, RM449012883GB shows scanned into our Swindon returns warehouse on the fifth of October, so there is definitely no unreturned equipment charge involved.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, well that's a relief at least. So why did it charge me the ten months of early termination fees?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at the disconnection order from the thirtieth of September, the previous agent keyed the cease reason code as 'Customer Voluntary Cease' instead of 'Home Move – Non-Serviceable Area'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh! So because they ticked the wrong box on the disconnection order, the computer thought I just cancelled for no reason?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is exactly what happened, Nafisa. Because 'Voluntary Cease' was selected on HM-774120, the billing run automatically charged twenty-four pounds per month for the ten months remaining.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do you have to transfer me back to the home-move department or retentions to get that code changed and the charge wiped off?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, I am not going to transfer you or make you explain this all over again, Nafisa. I am taking full ownership of verifying the wholesale database and wiping this charge myself today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, thank goodness! I was dreading being passed around three different departments.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I wouldn't put you through that. Under Ofcom rules and S-Net's Home Move policy, if neither S-Net LLU nor our partnered Openreach FTTP network serves your new postcode, the early termination charge is 100 percent waived.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, the only thing available up our lane in Bethesda is a fixed wireless dish through a local Welsh rural scheme.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me run the official Ofcom wholesale line plant check on LL57 4BQ and apply the manual waiver credit directly onto your live billing ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, sure, take whatever time you need.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me for a moment while I query the wholesale postcode database and get the two hundred and forty pound exemption credit posted to your final bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No problem at all, Zara, I'll hold.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much for holding, Nafisa! I have completed the wholesale coverage verification and updated your account ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant! Did the database confirm that S-Net doesn't cover Bryn Awel Cottage at LL57 4BQ?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it confirmed that LL57 4BQ is served only by an exchange-only copper line over six kilometres long that falls below S-Net's minimum guaranteed speed threshold, with zero FTTP footprint.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, that's what the first advisor told me back on the eighteenth of September.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So I have recoded cease order HM-774120 to 'Home Move – Non-Serviceable Postcode Exemption' and attached your Gwynedd Council Tax certificate to the audit trail.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about the actual two hundred and forty pound charge that was due to come out of my bank by Direct Debit next week?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have applied an immediate credit adjustment of two hundred and forty pounds and zero pence under credit note reference CN-8830419, and I also cancelled the pending Direct Debit collection request with your bank.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, so my bank won't have the two hundred and forty pounds taken out on the twenty-fourth of October?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not a penny will be taken, Nafisa. Because the final pro-rata line rental up to the thirtieth of September was already covered by your September payment, your closing balance is now exactly zero pounds and zero pence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, you have no idea what a weight off my shoulders that is, Zara!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm so glad we could get that stress off your plate! Do you happen to have the S-Net app or your online account portal open on your phone right now, Nafisa?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Uh, yes, I actually have the S-Net app open on my mobile from when I was looking at the bill earlier.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you pull down to refresh the 'Bills & Payments' screen in the app right now, let's check together that the revised final statement PDF has generated.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, let me refresh the screen... oh! A new entry just popped up dated today called Credit Note CN-8830419 for minus two hundred and forty pounds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what does the big 'Total Amount Due' banner at the top of your screen show now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says 'Total Amount Due: £0.00 – Account Closed & Settled in Full', and under Upcoming Direct Debit it says 'None scheduled'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you tap 'Download Revised Final Statement PDF', does it list the non-serviceable postcode waiver for LL57 4BQ on page one?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me open the PDF... yes, it says Early Termination Charge Waived – Non-Serviceable Home Move (LL57 4BQ), Balance £0.00! That is completely sorted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic, I have also emailed a copy of that revised zero-balance final statement and credit note CN-8830419 to your registered email address for your records.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Zara. Can I also double-check that my old address at Flat 4, 19 Clarendon Road isn't still set as my postal forwarding address on the closed file?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good catch—let me check the correspondence address field. I have just updated your forwarding postal address from Clarendon Road in Leeds to Bryn Awel Cottage, Bethesda, LL57 4BQ.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Awesome, that way no paper statements go to the new tenants in Leeds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. And since our Swindon warehouse already logged your Hub 5 return under RM449012883GB, your equipment record is marked 'Returned & Complete' as well.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So there is literally nothing else that could generate another bill or charge on this account in the future?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Nothing at all, Nafisa. The account status is permanently locked at 'Closed – Zero Balance', and no further billing cycles can run.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I cancel my S-Net Direct Debit mandate inside my banking app now, or leave it alone?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Since your balance is zero and the account is settled in full, you are completely free to cancel the dormant Direct Debit mandate in your banking app whenever you like.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, I will do that right after we finish speaking so my bank list stays tidy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a very sensible idea. I have also added a permanent audit note on your profile confirming that no early termination or equipment fees apply.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have been an absolute star today, Zara. Usually when something goes wrong with a telecom bill it takes three phone calls to fix.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Nafisa! Moving house is tiring enough without having to chase up an erroneous cancellation fee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Too right! Now I can actually get back to unpacking my saucepans in peace.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Enjoy the mountain views in Bethesda once those boxes are cleared! Before we wrap up, can I confirm you're 100 percent happy that the two hundred and forty pound charge is resolved today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 100 percent resolved, I'm looking right at the £0.00 balance on my phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else at all I can help you with today, Nafisa?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that is everything, thank you so much for all your help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just for your notebook, your credit note reference is CN-8830419 against home-move reference HM-774120, and the confirmation email should already be in your inbox.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my phone just pinged with the email from S-Net Billing confirming the zero balance!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful, everything is synced up across both the app and your email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks again, Zara, I really appreciate you sorting it out directly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was an absolute pleasure helping you today, Nafisa. We hope S-Net expands full-fibre out to your part of North Wales in the future!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If you ever bring fibre up our valley, I'll be the first to sign back up!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Nafisa, and if you have a moment after the call, there is a short survey on the service I provided today. Take care!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll definitely give you top marks on the survey. Bye now!
